09 / 21 · Projection

Stacked projections

A service graph can feed a capability graph. The service projection groups infrastructure details into the entities and relationships used by the capability projection.

Contract illustration
Master graphProjection
◉ Active+ Added− RemovedΔ Changed× Rejected
The rule
What the contract requires
Graph inputs name their source projection and expected ontology. Ordinary dependencies form an acyclic graph rooted at the master.
The boundary
Scope and constraints
Reverse lens edits use a separate command path. The forward graph dependencies remain acyclic.
Example · C#
Master, stacked and combined graphs
Full source ↗
One definition binds the master, a service view and a business view that consumes both.
UsageExamples.cs
public static GraphSpaceDefinition Compose(
    ProjectionDefinition ingestion, ProjectionDefinition services,
    ProjectionDefinition business)
{
    // services declares a "master" input; business declares "services"
    // and "inventory" inputs. Their operators consume those exact names.
    return new("1.0", "operations",
        new MasterGraphDefinition(new GraphId("master"), ingestion),
        [
            new(new GraphId("services"), services,
                [new("master", new MasterGraphSource(), ingestion.Ontology)]),
            new(new GraphId("business"), business,
                [new("services", new ProjectionGraphSource(services.Id), services.Ontology),
                 new("inventory", new MasterGraphSource(), ingestion.Ontology)])
        ]);
    // Each definition pins its own output ontology. The graph-space
    // compiler still validates the named bindings, operators and types.
}
Compile-checked caller example. Execution requires implementations of the injected interfaces.
